import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_0.csv",  # Source3_52_0
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_1.csv",  # Source3_52_1
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_2.csv",  # Source3_52_2
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_3.csv",  # Source3_52_3
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)  # Debt Collection Agency
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)  # Sidewalk Cafe
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)  # Pawnbroker
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)  # Cigarette Retail Dealer

# Rename columns in each dataframe to reflect their role in the target schema
# Target schema columns:
# ['zipcode': int,
#  'businesses_x': string, 'counts_x': int,
#  'businesses_y': string, 'counts_y': int,
#  'businesses_x_5': string, 'counts_x_6': int,
#  'businesses_y_7': string, 'counts_y_8': int]

# According to the target examples:
# - businesses_x and counts_x come from Source1 (Sidewalk Cafe)
# - businesses_y and counts_y come from Source2 (Pawnbroker)
# - businesses_x_5 and counts_x_6 come from Source0 (Debt Collection Agency)
# - businesses_y_7 and counts_y_8 come from Source3 (Cigarette Retail Dealer)

# So we rename the 'businesses' and 'counts' columns accordingly

df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_x_5',
    'counts': 'counts_x_6'
})

df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_x',
    'counts': 'counts_x'
})

df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_y',
    'counts': 'counts_y'
})

df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_y_7',
    'counts': 'counts_y_8'
})

# Now join all four dataframes on 'zipcode'
# Use outer join to keep all zipcodes from all sources
df_joined = df1_renamed.merge(df2_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer') \
                       .merge(df0_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer') \
                       .merge(df3_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Ensure the column order matches the target schema
target_columns = [
    'zipcode',
    'businesses_x', 'counts_x',
    'businesses_y', 'counts_y',
    'businesses_x_5', 'counts_x_6',
    'businesses_y_7', 'counts_y_8'
]

# Some zipcodes may have missing values in some columns due to outer join
# Fill missing string columns with empty string and integer columns with 0
# Identify string and integer columns based on target schema

string_cols = [
    'businesses_x',
    'businesses_y',
    'businesses_x_5',
    'businesses_y_7'
]

int_cols = [
    'counts_x',
    'counts_y',
    'counts_x_6',
    'counts_y_8'
]

# Fill missing values accordingly
df_joined[string_cols] = df_joined[string_cols].fillna('')
df_joined[int_cols] = df_joined[int_cols].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Reorder columns
df_final = df_joined[target_columns]

# Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
s0 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_0.csv', index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_1.csv', index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_2.csv', index_col=0)
s3 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/training_3.csv', index_col=0)

# Rename columns to match target schema parts before join
# For s1 and s2 join: businesses_x, counts_x from s1; businesses_y, counts_y from s2
s1_renamed = s1.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_x', 'counts': 'counts_x'})
s2_renamed = s2.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_y', 'counts': 'counts_y'})

# Join s1 and s2 on zipcode (inner join)
s1_s2 = pd.merge(s1_renamed, s2_renamed, on='zipcode', how='inner')

# For s0 and s3 join: businesses_x_5, counts_x_6 from s0; businesses_y_7, counts_y_8 from s3
s0_renamed = s0.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_x_5', 'counts': 'counts_x_6'})
s3_renamed = s3.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_y_7', 'counts': 'counts_y_8'})

# Join s0 and s3 on zipcode (inner join)
s0_s3 = pd.merge(s0_renamed, s3_renamed, on='zipcode', how='inner')

# Join the two joined tables on zipcode (inner join)
final_join = pd.merge(s1_s2, s0_s3, on='zipcode', how='inner')

# Group by the leftmost string/integer columns that appear unique and are keys in target:
# zipcode, businesses_x, businesses_y, businesses_x_5, businesses_y_7
# Aggregate counts columns by sum
grouped = final_join.groupby(
    ['zipcode', 'businesses_x', 'businesses_y', 'businesses_x_5', 'businesses_y_7'],
    as_index=False
).agg({
    'counts_x': 'sum',
    'counts_y': 'sum',
    'counts_x_6': 'sum',
    'counts_y_8': 'sum'
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[
    ['zipcode', 'businesses_x', 'counts_x', 'businesses_y', 'counts_y',
     'businesses_x_5', 'counts_x_6', 'businesses_y_7', 'counts_y_8']
]

# Write to output CSV
final_df.to_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_52/target_multisource_critique_history.csv', index=False)
